analysis:
The PR touches only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the last-updated date (line 3) and adds a paragraph (head lines 252-259) on SSD-stage behavior. The new text says SSD staging runs before engine.submit, off the engine queue, and that a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates its destinations already available from host bytes, never evaluating or fencing them, so staging does not wait on MLX-Swift's process-wide evalLock. It cites CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift and the SSD KV cache reference. No source code, crypto, authorization or wire behavior changed in the supplied evidence, so there is no direct security regression.

Relevant threats are T-041 (prefix-cache and SSD tier), T-010 and T-029 (availability), and TB-007. The change describes an availability and latency improvement: staging does not block on another request's prefill.

Unverified contract: the implementing change to CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift and the destination contract in ssd-kv-cache.md are outside the supplied evidence. A later pass should confirm that destinations created without eval or fence cannot be read before the host bytes are ready, and that AES-GCM authentication and the cacheSalt and HMAC lookup-tag scoping are still checked before import. The paragraph does not claim to change those mitigations, and T-041 posture appears unchanged: HMAC-keyed names, 30-minute TTL and account-scoped salt. Docs-only evidence is not proof of a regression, so no finding is raised.
